nodes.label: A man in his 40s presented with a 3-month history of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla
The patient reported severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night

Physical examination revealed 3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion limited to the right axilla; no other lesions were noted on skin or mucous membranes; Wood lamp examination was negative
The patient denied recent trauma, history of similar lesions, associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms; medical history was unremarkable; no environmental triggers or new medications
Treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement
Skin biopsy with histopathology, immunohistochemistry, TCR gene rearrangement, and flow cytometry has been requested but results are pending
CBC with differential, peripheral smear, and serum LDH have been ordered to assess systemic involvement but results are not yet available
The right axillary lesion is mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma)
Staging imaging (e.g., CT/PET) has been recommended but results are not yet available
Primary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder (e.g., primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma)
Other cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (e.g., Sézary syndrome, peripheral T-cell lymphoma)
H&E of skin biopsy shows epidermotropism
Peripheral blood flow cytometry has been requested but results are not yet available
